name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=string, descriptor=resource_filename_fdtxt_dat; reflects datatype (a NUL-terminated string constant). 'fdtxt' and 'dat' are the literal filename components of FDTXT.DAT (domain-meaningful), not Ghidra address residue, so they must stay. The name carries NO hex address suffix (unlike sibling _fdfield_dat_51a59), which is correct -- the convention forbids adding address residue. No change needed.
purpose: Read-only ASCII filename string "FDTXT.DAT" (10 bytes incl NUL); passed as the first (path) argument to fd2_load_dat_resource to open the chapter/dialog text archive FDTXT.DAT.
logic_summary: Static const char[10] = {'F','D','T','X','T','.','D','A','T',0}. Its address is taken (array decays to char*) and handed to fd2_load_dat_resource(filename, dst, idx). Three readers: main @0x25D07 loads idx 0 -> data_fd2_all_game_text_ptr (whole-game text blob); fd2_load_save_and_init_engine @0x101E9 and fd2_load_chapter_battle_data @0x108B7 each load idx (current_chapter_id + 1) -> data_fd2_current_chapter_text (per-chapter text). All three are DATA reads; the string itself is never modified. Immediately precedes "FDOTHER.DAT" @0x51A4D in the packed resource-filename string pool.
element_semantics: Each byte is one ASCII character of the path literal "FDTXT.DAT"; byte[9]=0x00 is the C string terminator. Consumed whole as a char* file path, not indexed element-wise.
notes: src comment (strtab.c lines 59-67) was already accurate, precise, conclusion-style ASCII; verified verbatim against all 3 caller decompiles (idx 0 -> all-game-text in main; idx chapter+1 -> current-chapter-text in fd2_load_save_and_init_engine and fd2_load_chapter_battle_data) and against memory bytes 46 44 54 58 54 2e 44 41 54 00 = 'FDTXT.DAT\0'. No edit to src needed (comment kept). Ghidra data plate was NULL -> created a concise plate matching the src conclusion via run_script_inline cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...) (MCP set_plate_comment fails on data). is_const=true: zero game-side write-xrefs, all 3 xrefs are DATA reads taking the address as a char* path. No logic issues.
